header.stance: 核心 CPI 給 Fed 更多時間，油價與借款需求仍推高長端利率

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 核心 CPI 較溫和，長天期美債仍未上漲

美國核心通膨週三帶來一些緩解，卻不足以讓美債漲勢維持。2 年期殖利率在數據公布後一度降向 4.11%，收盤仍持平於 4.13%；股市雖然下跌，10 年與 30 年期殖利率反而各上升 2 個基點至 4.55% 與 5.03%。

5 月核心消費者物價月增 0.2%，低於市場預估的 0.3%，整體通膨年增率則達 4.2%，為三年來最快。這讓 Fed 有更多時間觀察能源衝擊，但交換市場仍反映 12 月升息。隨後原油庫存降幅超過預期，油價上漲，實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率也都小幅走高。

市場並非沒有需求。$390 億 10 年期增額標售的得標殖利率略低於發行前交易，間接投標人取得超過四分之三，交易商不到一成。然而，超乎預期的聯邦赤字與創紀錄的全球主權發行，仍使整體借款前景受到關注。企業交易也呈現相同張力：Amazon 與 AI 計畫取得大筆資金，供給卻迫使投資組合調整，弱勢借款人的融資代價則高得多。

## 通膨緩解遇上油價與財政壓力

核心 CPI 顯示，較高油價尚未擴散為普遍的月度物價上升。但強勁就業與整體通膨，仍使交易員預期 Fed 在 12 月前升息。單月核心數據良好，降低了提早行動的迫切性，卻還不能確定目前 3.50%–3.75% 政策區間足以抑制需求與成本壓力。

美債跌幅隨天期增加。5 年期殖利率上升 1 個基點至 4.27%，2 年期不變、長端上升，使 2s10s 擴大 2 個基點至 42 個基點，2s30s 擴大 2 個基點至 90 個基點。2s5s10s 蝶式利差維持 −14 個基點，2s10s30s 則因 10 年期相對兩翼略弱，上升 2 個基點至 −6 個基點。

累積變動仍以前端與中段較大。2 年、5 年、10 年與 30 年期殖利率一週升幅分別為 5、6、6 與 4 個基點，一個月升幅為 23、25、17 與 8 個基點。過去一個月，2s10s 仍趨平 6 個基點，2s30s 趨平 15 個基點。

10 年期實質殖利率上升 1 個基點至 2.21%，損益兩平通膨率上升 1 個基點至 2.34%，回吐部分週二的通膨補償降幅。5 年期實質殖利率上升 1 個基點至 1.83%，7 年期上升 2 個基點至 2.02%，20 年與 30 年期則分別上升 2 與 3 個基點至 2.58% 與 2.78%。

油價提供了保持審慎的理由。WTI 上漲 2.07% 至 $90.03，布蘭特上漲 1.80% 至 $93.10。美國商業原油庫存減少 722.7 萬桶，遠超預期的 397.4 萬桶，降至 4.265 億桶，較季節性五年平均低約 5%。包括戰略石油儲備的總石油庫存減少 1,350 萬桶，煉油產能利用率達 95.3%。

10 年期標售則為存續期間買家帶來較好的結果。$390 億增額發行以 4.538% 得標，比 4.539% 的發行前交易低 0.1 個基點，投標倍數 2.57。競爭性得標分配中，間接投標人取得 78.21%，直接投標人 12.32%，交易商 9.46%。票息 4.375% 的券種將在 6 月 15 日交割。最終投資人參與強勁，使當日溫和的長端賣壓沒有因供給進一步擴大。

聯邦收支則顯示，這場標售還無法結束更大的財政討論。5 月赤字 $2,926.5 億，高於預估的 $2,695 億，4 月則為盈餘 $2,150.2 億。收入 $3,355.1 億、支出 $6,281.6 億，使會計年度至今赤字達 $1.246 兆。單次增額發行需求良好，累積融資需求仍然龐大。

現金市場保持穩定。4 週與 6 週券債券等值殖利率各上升 1 個基點至 3.67% 與 3.68%，8 週券持平於 3.68%；13 週與 26 週券分別維持 3.72% 與 3.81%，52 週券維持 3.90%。

## 大型 AI 融資改變信用投資組合

信用債 ETF 跌幅遠小於股票。LQD 下跌 0.23%、HYG 下跌 0.19%、JNK 下跌 0.20%，相較之下，S&P 500 下跌 1.62%、Nasdaq 100 下跌 1.98%、半導體下跌 3.57%。VIX 上升 11.83% 至 22.22；美元指數幾乎持平，上漲 0.04% 至 99.95，黃金下跌 3.56% 至 $4,108.20。股市賣壓並未換得較低的長天期美債殖利率。

Amazon 的加拿大融資，呈現成功發行如何對相鄰券種形成壓力。週一定價的 C$140 億、五批次發行，是史上最大加幣公司債，使 Amazon 躋身當地指數前十大發行人。其中 C$47.5 億 30 年期，單一批次就超過加拿大政府長債常見的 C$30 億標售。基金經理賣出公用事業、Alphabet 債券及其他高品質持倉，以騰出額度。

交易後，加拿大公司債相對公債利差擴大約 2 個基點至 84.5 個基點，但仍比五年平均窄逾 30%。考量發行規模與強勁基金流入，變動不大；交易商卻預期，投資組合恢復承接能力前，其他大型借款人可能延後發行。交易前後，加拿大長期公債也落後同天期美債。

Amazon 另取得花旗主導的 $175 億無擔保延遲動用定期貸款，增加流動性來源。額度可用至 9 月底，每次動用有三年還款期，依優先無擔保評等，以 SOFR 加 62.5 至 87.5 個基點計價。這可作為潛在 AI 股權投資承諾的過渡資金，無須立即再發債。

部分 CoreWeave 相關資產，計畫融資投資人接受的殖利率也明顯降低。Applied Digital 子公司發行 $15.9 億 2031 年債券，以 7% 殖利率在北達科他興建另一座租給 CoreWeave 的設施，前一階段融資成本則為 10%。訂單約達發行額五倍，15 年租約與投資人對租戶信用觀感改善支撐交易，所得也用於償還過橋貸款。

CoreWeave 五年期違約保障成本由 12 月的 8.81 個百分點降至 4.52 個百分點。開發商已為租給它的計畫籌得逾 $80 億，CoreWeave 本身也準備等值 $35 億的美元與歐元發行。租戶信用改善可以降低計畫成本，但這條擴大的融資鏈，仍共同仰賴使用率、客戶集中度與持續籌資能力等假設。

花旗研究凸顯，租戶名稱之下的契約同樣重要。一檔與 Microsoft 有關、不分期攤還的 QTS 資料中心債，表現已偏離 Microsoft 公司債；另外四筆大型計畫交易則跟隨保證人或直接租戶。即使租戶評等高，攤還安排、租約與計畫層級回收仍不能忽略。

Oracle 收盤後財報又增加未來供給。季度資本支出 $165 億，全年 $557 億，高於原計畫 $500 億，此前已籌得 $430 億債務與 $50 億股權資金。新會計年度預計淨資本支出約 $700 億，並再籌 $400 億債務與股權資金。

日本製鐵則為併購風險付出更高價格。收購美國鋼鐵後首次一般公司債發行，籌得 ¥900 億；10 年期票息 3.202%，相對日債利差 54 個基點，為 1998 年以來最寬。投資人參與廣泛使規模得以增加，但日本利率上升與收購帶來的營運、資產負債表風險，也要求更多讓利。

強勢發行人之外，融資彈性正在惡化。Pimco 指出，投資等級利差仍接近近三十年最窄水準，槓桿與民間信貸卻愈來愈常延長到期日、以增加本金的方式付息。收盤後報導顯示，全球 CCC 債相對較高品質高收益債的額外殖利率達約 6.4 個百分點，創 14 個月高點。Pimco 與其他投資人將壓力連結至成長放緩、再融資昂貴，以及約 $2 兆收購熱潮所形成的融資結構。弱勢借款人面臨現金生成下降與資金成本上升同時發生。

佛羅里達州收盤後新增另一項市政債風險。擬議修憲將自用住宅免稅額由 $5 萬提高至 2027 年 $15 萬、2028 年最高 $25 萬，估計 60% 房屋將完全免繳房產稅，需在 2026 年 11 月獲 60% 選民支持。S&P 警告，部分地方發行人收入與支出可能面臨重大壓力；全州未償市政債超過 $1,750 億。依賴受影響稅基的債券，需要替代收入或支出調整來維持償債保障。

## 海外供給檢驗買盤，成長訊號仍分歧

日本 30 年期標售投標倍數 2.94，低於前次 3.49，也低於過去一年平均 3.4，債券期貨在標售後擴大跌幅。殖利率回落後，投資人更不願增加超長期部位，通膨、財政不確定性與日銀可能減少購債，仍壓抑需求。

總裁植田和男住院，並未明顯降低市場對日銀再次升息的預期。副總裁接手主持與對外溝通，預期的委員會決策大致未變。對日本機構而言，國內報酬可能提高，使海外配置更取決於避險成本與波動。

2026 年全球政府透過聯合承銷發行已籌得創紀錄的 $5,040 億，高於疫情期間同期，另有大量例行標售。義大利占近 €700 億，德國在放寬國防與基建財政規則後籌得 €140 億。需求尤其集中較短天期，使債務管理單位得以提前融資，但戰爭與政策不確定性也要求更高殖利率。

歐元區透過聯合承銷進行的再融資年增 26%，總發行量則增 11%。5 月贖回減少，發行卻加快，顯示部分借款可能在潛在升息前提前進行。成功發行代表市場仍有儲蓄資金，也讓國際投資組合擁有更多高評等替代選擇。

歐洲財政委員會反對把未使用的國防支出彈性，轉為普遍性的能源補助。各國到 2028 年每年可動用最高 GDP 的 0.3%，三年上限 0.6%。委員會援引 2022–2023 年經驗，認為未精準鎖定對象的支持，可能刺激需求與通膨，使 ECB 必須加大緊縮，即使政府原意是保護家庭。

加拿大在經濟連續兩季萎縮後，第五次連續維持隔夜利率 2.25%。總裁 Tiff Macklem 表示，重大的新增美國貿易限制可能需要寬鬆，持續的能源轉嫁則可能需要連續升息。債市更在意景氣疲弱，2 年期殖利率由盤中高點約 2.882%，在決策後降至約 2.836%。成長、閒置產能與基礎物價未予確認時，重複的緊縮警告影響有限。

中國 5 月數據則呈現消費通膨偏弱、工廠成本較強。CPI 月減 0.1%、年增 1.2%，低於預估的 1.4%，核心通膨降至 1.1%；PPI 月增 0.5%、年增 3.9%，高於預估的 3.5%，能源、金屬與其他投入成本仍強。消費疲弱支持政策援助，上游成本升高卻使金融情勢放鬆的路徑更複雜。

## 匯率防衛與債務修復，左右新興市場

印尼在急跌後收復部分失土。10 年期殖利率下跌 15 個基點至 7.26%，此前兩天一度累計上升 64 個基點；印尼盾最多上漲 0.9%，股票上漲 3.4%。央行與財政部的保證減緩賣壓，但外資今年仍自債市淨撤出 $5.94 億、自股市撤出 $37 億。

印尼央行表示，願容許較高債券殖利率來防衛匯率，不買進 10 年以上券種，透過附買回工具抽走銀行流動性，並降低外資避險成本；財政部長重申赤字法定上限為 GDP 的 3%。措施讓匯率防衛方向更明確，卻也提高政府融資成本，同時進口油價上升增加燃料補貼需求。

土耳其尚未調整帳面利率，金融條件卻已收緊。多數經濟學家預期一週附買回利率第三次維持 37%，但該管道已暫停，銀行改以接近 40% 的隔夜利率融資。戰爭爆發以來，外匯準備總額減少 $200 億，當局透過出售黃金或交換交易抵抗里拉貶值。通膨連續兩個月加快，年底市場預估接近 30%，高於央行的 26%。正式利率不變，仍意味昂貴融資持續。

DP World 的再融資計畫，呈現衝突對企業借款人的影響。Jebel Ali 港前三個月貨量下跌 30%，管理層在 9 月 €7.5 億到期前與債券投資人會面。公司可用現金償還，但戰爭爆發後一直未發行，現在考慮市場再融資。$10 億 2029 年債券 3 月曾跌至 94.9 美分，目前約 95.6。流動性降低眼前還款風險，貨量轉弱與新發行價格則決定較長期成本。

南非準備銀行警告，衝突若延續，可能加重家庭壓力、違約與不良貸款。央行 5 月升息 25 個基點至 7%，為三年來首次，並將第三季通膨預測由 3.7% 上修至 4.9%。能源變貴不只影響通膨，也影響銀行未來的信用品質。

迦納重整後復甦較強。第一季 GDP 年增 6.4%，前季為 5.8%，財政改革與較低借款成本抵銷部分戰爭衝擊。政府將 2026 年成長預測由 4.8% 上修至逾 6%，2022 年違約後的 IMF 支持調整仍持續。通膨 3.7% 遠低於一年前 18.4%，但燃料已使其連續第二個月上升。央行在前一年由 28% 降息後，維持 14%，權衡較佳成長、償債能力與再起的物價壓力。

紐約截止時間後，S&P 將阿根廷由 CCC+ 升至 B−、展望穩定，理由包括財政盈餘、準備累積與外部流動性改善。央行今年已買進逾 $100 億準備，本地美元發行與多邊融資則覆蓋近期需求。升評改善重返國際借款與負債管理的前景，但發生在當日收盤之後；此前美債殖利率與油價上升，使 EMB 下跌 0.33%。

## 接著看 PPI 與長債標售

PPI 與初領失業金在 6 月 11 日美東 08:30 公布。整體生產者物價月增率預估由 1.4% 降至 0.7%，核心由 1.0% 降至 0.5%；初領預測介於 21.6 萬至 22 萬人，前次為 22.5 萬人。上游通膨放緩、就業轉弱，會強化 Fed 等待的理由；核心物價仍強且初領偏低，則意味週三 CPI 緩解太有限，還不足以改變升息路徑。

財政部將在美東 11:30 分別標售 $750 億 4 週與 8 週券，13:00 增額發行 $220 億 30 年期，並可能在 13:40–14:00 買回最高 $125 億近端名目附息債。長債得標利率相對發行前交易、投標人比重與交易商承接，將呈現 10 年期的強勁需求能否延伸。國庫券需求與 6 月 15 日附息債交割，則是不同的現金測試。若通膨溫和、長債需求卻弱，供給壓力將再次受到關注。

ECB 與土耳其在 6 月 11 日決策，日銀會議於 16 日結束。基本預期是 ECB 升息 25 個基點、存款利率至 2.25%，土耳其附買回利率維持 37%、實際融資接近 40%，日銀升息 25 個基點至約 1.00%。除了德債、日債、里拉與日圓走勢，後續政策指引與日銀購債計畫同樣重要。曲線有序、匯率穩定，有助降低國際長債壓力；若準備再流失或長端出現賣壓，則指向相反結果。

overall_summary.headline: 核心 CPI 較溫和，長天期美債仍未上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
5 月核心 CPI 月增 0.2%，低於預估的 0.3%，整體通膨年增率則達 4.2%。2 年期殖利率一度接近 4.11%，收盤持平於 4.13%；10 年期上升 2 個基點至 4.55%。原油庫存大減推高油價，實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率也都上升。

$390 億 10 年期標售得標利率低於發行前交易 0.1 個基點，間接投標人取得 78.21%。然而，5 月聯邦赤字 $2,926.5 億與創紀錄的全球主權聯合承銷發行，仍使長期借款需求受到關注。Amazon 加幣交易迫使投資組合調整，Applied Digital 取得較便宜的計畫融資，弱勢 CCC 借款人的額外殖利率卻擴大。

股市重挫仍未帶動美債上漲。加拿大維持利率、債券回升，日本 30 年期需求卻轉弱。印尼急跌後初步穩定，阿根廷升評則在收盤後公布。接著看 PPI、初領失業金、30 年期增額發行與海外央行指引。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Softer Core CPI Fails to Lift Long Treasuries

US core inflation offered some relief on Wednesday, but it was not enough to sustain a Treasury rally. The 2-year yield briefly fell toward 4.11% after the release before closing unchanged at 4.13%. The 10- and 30-year yields instead rose 2 basis points to 4.55% and 5.03%, even as stocks sold off.

Core consumer prices rose 0.2% in May, below the 0.3% consensus, while headline inflation reached 4.2% year on year, its fastest pace in three years. The result gave the Fed more time to assess the energy shock without dislodging a December increase from swap pricing. Oil then rose alongside a larger-than-expected inventory draw, and both real yields and breakevens edged higher.

Demand was not absent. The $39 billion 10-year reopening cleared just through its when-issued yield, with indirect buyers taking more than three-quarters and dealers less than a tenth. Yet a wider-than-expected federal deficit and record global sovereign issuance kept the broader borrowing outlook in view. Corporate transactions showed the same tension: Amazon and AI projects secured large sums, while the supply forced portfolio adjustments and weaker borrowers paid much more for access.

## Inflation Relief Meets Oil and Fiscal Pressure

The core CPI result suggested that higher oil had not yet spread into a broad monthly inflation impulse. Strong hiring and headline inflation nevertheless left traders pricing a Fed increase by December. A favorable core month reduced the urgency of an earlier move, but did not settle whether the current 3.50%–3.75% policy range would contain demand and cost pressures.

Treasury losses grew with maturity. The 5-year yield added 1 basis point to 4.27%, while the unchanged 2-year and higher long yields steepened 2s10s by 2 basis points to 42 and 2s30s by 2 to 90. The 2s5s10s butterfly held at −14; 2s10s30s rose 2 basis points to −6 as the 10-year modestly underperformed its wings.

The accumulated move remained larger at the front and belly. Weekly increases in 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were 5, 6, 6 and 4 basis points, while monthly increases were 23, 25, 17 and 8. Over the month, 2s10s was still 6 basis points flatter and 2s30s 15 flatter.

The 10-year real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.21% and its breakeven added 1 to 2.34%, reversing part of Tuesday's inflation-premium decline. Five-year real yields increased 1 basis point to 1.83%, seven-year yields rose 2 to 2.02%, and the 20- and 30-year real yields gained 2 and 3 basis points to 2.58% and 2.78%.

Oil supplied a reason for continued caution. WTI rose 2.07% to $90.03 and Brent gained 1.80% to $93.10. US commercial crude inventories fell 7.227 million barrels, far more than the 3.974 million decline expected, to 426.5 million barrels, about 5% below the seasonal five-year average. Total petroleum stocks including the Strategic Petroleum Reserve dropped 13.5 million barrels, while refinery utilization reached 95.3%.

The 10-year auction provided a better result for buyers of duration. The $39 billion reopening stopped at 4.538%, 0.1 basis point through the 4.539% when-issued level, with bid-to-cover of 2.57. Indirect bidders took 78.21% of accepted competitive awards, direct bidders 12.32% and dealers 9.46%. The 4.375% notes settle June 15. Strong end-user participation contained the immediate supply risk during a session of mild long-end cheapening.

The federal accounts showed why that result did not close the larger fiscal debate. May's deficit was $292.65 billion, above the $269.5 billion consensus, following April's $215.02 billion surplus. Receipts of $335.51 billion and outlays of $628.16 billion brought the fiscal-year-to-date shortfall to $1.246 trillion. One well-received reopening left the cumulative financing requirement substantial.

Cash conditions remained steady. Four- and six-week coupon-equivalent bill yields rose 1 basis point to 3.67% and 3.68%, while the eight-week held at 3.68%. The 13- and 26-week yields were unchanged at 3.72% and 3.81%; the 52-week remained at 3.90%.

## Large AI Financings Reshape Credit Portfolios

Credit funds fell much less than equities. LQD lost 0.23%, HYG 0.19% and JNK 0.20%, against declines of 1.62% in the S&P 500, 1.98% in Nasdaq 100 and 3.57% in semiconductors. VIX rose 11.83% to 22.22. The dollar index was nearly flat, up 0.04% at 99.95, while gold fell 3.56% to $4,108.20. The stock selloff did not translate into lower long Treasury yields.

Amazon's Canadian financing showed how a successful deal can put pressure on neighboring securities. Its C$14 billion, five-part sale, priced Monday, was the largest Canadian-dollar corporate bond offering and made it a top-ten issuer in the local index. The C$4.75 billion 30-year tranche alone exceeded a typical C$3 billion Canadian government long-bond auction. Managers sold utilities, Alphabet debt and other high-quality holdings to create room.

Canadian corporate spreads widened about 2 basis points after the transaction to 84.5 basis points over governments, still more than 30% tighter than their five-year average. The move was modest given the sale's size and strong fund inflows, but dealers expected other large borrowers to delay issuance while portfolios rebuilt capacity. Long Canadian government bonds had also underperformed comparable Treasuries around the deal.

Amazon added a separate source of liquidity with a $17.5 billion unsecured delayed-draw term loan led by Citigroup. The facility is available through September, each drawing has a three-year repayment period, and pricing ranges from 62.5 to 87.5 basis points over SOFR depending on its senior unsecured rating. It could bridge prospective AI equity commitments without requiring another immediate bond sale.

Project lenders also accepted substantially lower yields for some CoreWeave-linked assets. An Applied Digital subsidiary raised $1.59 billion of 2031 bonds at 7% to build another North Dakota facility leased to CoreWeave, compared with 10% for an earlier phase. Orders were about five times the deal size. A 15-year lease and improved perceptions of the tenant supported the sale; proceeds also repay a bridge loan.

CoreWeave's five-year default-protection cost had fallen to 4.52 percentage points from 8.81 in December. Developers had raised more than $8 billion for projects leased to it, while CoreWeave itself was preparing a $3.5 billion-equivalent dollar-and-euro offering. Better tenant credit can lower project financing costs, but the expanding chain still depends on related assumptions about utilization, customer concentration and access to funding.

Citi's research highlighted the importance of the contract beneath the tenant name. A non-amortizing QTS data-center bond tied to Microsoft had diverged from Microsoft's corporate debt, while four other large project deals had tracked their guarantors or direct tenants. The difference leaves amortization, leases and project-level recovery important even when the tenant is highly rated.

Oracle's after-close results added to the prospective supply. Quarterly capital expenditure was $16.5 billion and annual spending $55.7 billion, above its $50 billion plan, following $43 billion of debt and $5 billion of equity raised. For the new fiscal year, Oracle expected roughly $70 billion of net capital spending and another $40 billion of debt and equity financing.

Nippon Steel paid more for acquisition risk. It raised ¥90 billion in its first straight-bond sale since buying US Steel. The 10-year tranche carried a 3.202% coupon and a 54-basis-point spread over JGBs, its widest since 1998. Broad investor interest allowed an increased deal size, but higher local rates and the acquisition's business and balance-sheet risks required a wider concession.

Below the stronger issuers, financing flexibility was deteriorating. Pimco pointed to growing use of maturity extensions and payment-in-kind structures in leveraged and private credit while high-grade spreads remained near their tightest in almost three decades. After-close reporting put the extra yield on global CCC debt over better-quality junk at about 6.4 percentage points, a 14-month high. Pimco and other investors linked the pressure to slower growth, expensive refinancing and structures originating in a roughly $2 trillion buyout boom. These weaker borrowers face falling cash generation at the same time as funding costs rise.

Florida introduced a separate municipal risk after the close. A proposed constitutional amendment would raise the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and as much as $250,000 in 2028, eliminating property tax on an estimated 60% of homes. Approval requires 60% of voters in November 2026. S&P warned of material revenue and spending pressure for some local issuers, in a state with more than $175 billion of municipal debt outstanding. Bonds dependent on the affected tax base would need replacement revenues or spending adjustments to preserve coverage.

## Overseas Supply Tests Buyers as Growth Diverges

Japan's 30-year auction drew bid-to-cover of 2.94, down from 3.49 previously and below the prior year's 3.4 average. Bond futures extended losses after the sale. Buyers were less willing to add super-long duration following a yield pullback, with inflation, fiscal uncertainty and prospective reductions in BOJ purchases still weighing on demand.

Expectations for another BOJ increase remained strong despite Governor Kazuo Ueda's hospitalization. Deputies took over chairing and communication duties, without materially altering the expected board decision. For Japanese institutions, the prospect of higher domestic returns makes overseas allocation more sensitive to hedging costs and volatility.

Governments globally had raised a record $504 billion through syndications in 2026, above the comparable pandemic-era pace, with regular auctions adding much more borrowing. Italy accounted for nearly €70 billion and Germany €14 billion after relaxing fiscal rules for defense and infrastructure. Strong demand, particularly at shorter maturities, allowed debt managers to advance funding, albeit at higher yields amid war and policy uncertainty.

Euro-area refinancing through syndications rose 26% year on year, against an 11% increase in total syndicated issuance. May volumes accelerated even as redemptions fell, suggesting some funding was brought forward ahead of possible rate increases. Successful sales demonstrate available savings, but also create more high-grade alternatives for international portfolios.

The European Fiscal Board warned against using unused defense-spending flexibility for broad energy aid. Countries could deploy up to 0.3% of GDP annually through 2028, capped at 0.6% over three years. Drawing on the 2022–2023 experience, the board argued that untargeted support could stimulate demand and inflation, forcing the ECB to do more even as governments tried to cushion households.

Canada kept its overnight rate at 2.25% for a fifth consecutive meeting after two quarters of contraction. Governor Tiff Macklem said significant new US trade restrictions could require easing, while persistent energy pass-through might require consecutive increases. Bonds focused on the weak economy: the 2-year yield fell from an intraday high near 2.882% to about 2.836% after the decision. Repeated warnings about tightening carried less weight without confirmation from growth, spare capacity and underlying prices.

China's May data showed weak consumer inflation alongside stronger factory costs. CPI fell 0.1% monthly and rose 1.2% yearly, below the 1.4% consensus, while core inflation eased to 1.1%. PPI rose 0.5% monthly and 3.9% yearly, above the 3.5% forecast, as energy, metals and other inputs remained firm. Consumer weakness favored support, but higher upstream costs complicated the path toward easier financial conditions.

## Currency Defense and Debt Repair Shape EM

Indonesia recovered some ground after a severe selloff. Its 10-year yield fell 15 basis points to 7.26% after rising as much as 64 basis points over the preceding two days. The rupiah gained as much as 0.9% and stocks rose 3.4%. Reassurance from the central bank and finance ministry helped slow selling, although foreign investors had withdrawn a net $594 million from bonds and $3.7 billion from equities during the year.

Bank Indonesia said it would tolerate higher bond yields to defend the currency, avoid buying securities of ten years or longer, drain bank liquidity through repurchase facilities and reduce foreign investors' hedging costs. The finance minister reaffirmed the statutory deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP. The measures clarified the currency-defense approach, but raised the cost of financing the government while imported oil increased fuel-subsidy needs.

Türkiye was already tightening financial conditions without changing its headline rate. Most economists expected a third consecutive hold in the one-week repo rate at 37%, but access to that facility had been paused and banks were instead funding near the 40% overnight rate. Gross foreign-exchange reserves had fallen $20 billion since the war began, with gold sales or swaps used to resist lira weakness. Inflation had accelerated for two months, and year-end consensus near 30% exceeded the central bank's 26% forecast. A formal hold would therefore leave expensive funding in place.

DP World's refinancing plans showed the conflict's effect on a corporate borrower. Jebel Ali port volumes fell 30% in the first three months, and management met bond investors before a €750 million September maturity. It could repay from cash but was considering market refinancing after avoiding issuance since the war began. Its $1 billion 2029 bond, which fell to 94.9 cents in March, was around 95.6. Liquidity reduced immediate repayment risk; weaker volumes and the price of a new deal would determine the longer-term cost.

South Africa's reserve bank warned that prolonged conflict could increase household stress, defaults and nonperforming loans. It had raised rates 25 basis points to 7% in May, the first increase in three years, and lifted its third-quarter inflation forecast to 4.9% from 3.7%. More expensive energy was affecting not only the inflation outlook but also prospective bank credit quality.

Ghana's recovery after restructuring was stronger. First-quarter GDP grew 6.4% year on year, up from 5.8% in the preceding quarter, as fiscal reforms and lower borrowing costs offset part of the war shock. The government lifted its 2026 growth forecast above 6% from 4.8%, with the IMF-backed adjustment continuing after the 2022 default. Inflation at 3.7% was far below the year-earlier 18.4%, but fuel had pushed it higher for a second month. The central bank held at 14% after cutting from 28% over the previous year, balancing better growth and debt capacity against renewed price pressure.

After the New York cutoff, S&P upgraded Argentina to B− from CCC+ with a stable outlook, citing fiscal surpluses, reserve accumulation and improved external liquidity. The central bank had bought more than $10 billion of reserves during the year, while local dollar placements and multilateral funding covered near-term needs. The upgrade improves the prospective route to international borrowing and liability management. It followed, rather than explained, a session in which EMB fell 0.33% as higher Treasury yields and oil weighed on the common EM backdrop.

## PPI and the Long-Bond Auction Follow

PPI and initial claims arrive June 11 at 08:30 ET. Headline producer-price growth is forecast to slow to 0.7% monthly from 1.4%, and core to 0.5% from 1.0%; claims forecasts range from 216,000 to 220,000 after 225,000. Softer pipeline inflation combined with weaker hiring would strengthen the case for the Fed to wait. Firm core prices and low claims would suggest that Wednesday's CPI relief was too narrow to alter the expected hike path.

Treasury will sell $75 billion each of four- and eight-week bills at 11:30 ET, reopen $22 billion of 30-year bonds at 13:00, and may buy back up to $12.5 billion of near-term nominal coupons between 13:40 and 14:00. The long bond's clearing level against when-issued trading, bidder shares and dealer takedown will show whether the strong 10-year reception extends farther out. Bill demand and June 15 coupon settlement remain separate cash tests. Weak long-bond demand despite benign inflation would put supply pressure back in focus.

The ECB and Türkiye decide on June 11, followed by the BOJ meeting ending June 16. The base case is a 25-basis-point ECB increase taking the deposit rate to 2.25%, a Turkish repo hold at 37% with effective funding near 40%, and a 25-basis-point BOJ increase toward 1.00%. Guidance on further moves and the BOJ purchase plan will matter alongside Bund and JGB trading, the lira and yen. Orderly curves and stable currencies would ease some pressure on international duration; renewed reserve losses or long-end selling would point the other way.
